text: hey see ifu can solve this problem the camera feed is not rendering in the app but it detects the obs virt camera just fine, something is wrong [Image #1]

events.text: Root cause confirmed on live /dev/video42: the frame-thread MultiReader retained one byte of spare capacity and converged to tiny pipe reads, so it could not assemble a 3.69MB RGBA frame before the 10s watchdog killed FFmpeg. OBS also emitted native 1920x1080 bytes despite the 1280x720 input request. Fix uses a cancelable native-Io whole-frame pump with pointer swaps and pins FFmpeg output scaling to the renderer buffer size.

resolution: Fixed the black OBS Virtual Camera preview at the native capture boundary. The old frame-thread MultiReader advanced in tiny pipe chunks and never assembled a multi-megabyte RGBA frame before the watchdog killed FFmpeg; OBS also kept emitting its native 1920x1080 payload despite a 1280x720 input request. Capture now pins FFmpeg output to the renderer dimensions and drains complete frames on a cancelable native-Io worker, handing the newest frame to paint by pointer swap so the frame thread neither waits nor copies payloads. Added a full-frame subprocess regression test, verified exact live /dev/video42 byte counts, passed capture/pose/device tests and ReleaseFast editor ship, and completed a 60-second pose stress with zero frame-budget spikes.
